## The single weakest link (judgement of this task)

**U3/U5b: the deployed sink.ts, the only component that writes committed state.** It is not only unproved; it is known to be wrong. A machine-checked counterexample (U5r-CONTRAST) and Node runs show that it commits two intents with one request id and does not bind the intent charge id; the differentials (U5b, and the control pairs of U5v3-DIFF) confirm the real sink diverges from the V3 core. The night added repairs only as DRAFTS (T-V3, T-SHELLV3, T-BYTES-V3, T-RESTART, T-KEYED, sink_core_backed_v3.ts), none applied. Even the drafts rest on NO-ROLLBACK and AUTHENTIC-INIT, which no audit over the database can check, and on CREATE-AUTHORITY, which no deployed code enforces (U9, U10 MISSING). Runner-up: ADMISSION (S1, E1-E6): main is not protected and the deployed gate admits run-time halts (E6; the draft subset rule refuses them but also refuses 9 of 19 known-correct submissions).
